term: Illustrative Work Transformation / Weighted Propagation Matrix
statement: The WTM/propagation model is an illustrative test harness for evaluating the Predictive Program Management 2.0 architecture. Its weights are evidence-calibrated ordinal values and synthetic assumptions, not historically calibrated probabilities.
computed_by: ppm_agent.tools.wtm_tools (deterministic Python / numpy; no LLM involvement)
orientation: W[i, j]: row i = source / upstream node, column j = target / downstream node (DSM convention, unchanged)
equation: x(t+1) = W^T x(t), i.e. x_j(t+1) = sum_i W[i, j] * x_i(t)
transformations: W is the frozen weighted DSM (outputs/dsm/weighted_dsm.csv), read element by element with no scaling, normalization, thresholding or reordering.
W^T is used only inside the state update x(t+1) = W^T x(t), so that each target column sums its sources. It is not written to any file.
modelling_assumption: Ordinal DSM weights are used directly as multiplicative propagation coefficients.
initial_state_note: Normalized analytical disturbance; not a probability or a historical measurement.
stopping_rule: Fixed horizon: iterate from t0 to t6 as specified, with no early stopping. The long-run behaviour beyond the horizon is characterised analytically by the spectral radius and, because it is below 1, by the closed-form cumulative total (I - W^T)^-1 x(0).
behaviour_rule: step ratio = total(t) / total(t-1); > 1 + 0.05 AMPLIFYING, < 1 - 0.05 DECAYING, otherwise PERSISTENT.
numeric_precision: values rounded to 10 decimals in outputs
